key_insight: A multi-aspect, multi-agent multimodal system (MAMA-Memeia) plus the new RESTOREx resource enables more nuanced identification of depressive symptoms in memes by combining separate agents that specialize on text, image, and contextual cues.
problem_solved: Detecting depressive symptoms in memes is hard because meaning is conveyed jointly by images, overlaid text, and cultural/contextual signals; this work addresses noisy, multimodal, and subtle symptom indicators that single-stream models miss.
method: Design a multi-agent architecture where specialized agents analyze image content, overlaid text, and contextual metadata, then collaborate to form a unified symptom prediction.
Incorporate multi-aspect reasoning (literal text, visual cues, affective signals, and context) and aggregate agent outputs via an ensemble/coordination mechanism.

Introduce RESTOREx, a curated multimodal dataset/resource tailored for depressive-symptom labeling in memes and used to train and evaluate the system (leveraging LLMs/vision backbones for agent reasoning).
impact: Provides practitioners a practical multimodal modeling pattern and an annotated resource for building more sensitive, explainable depressive-symptom detectors in memes, enabling safer mental-health screening tools while highlighting the need for ethical safeguards.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: agents for text, image, and context feeding into a coordinator/ensemble
Example meme triplets: original meme + agent-level attention/highlight overlays (text focus, face/scene focus) + final prediction

paper_title: MAMA-Memeia! Multi-Aspect Multi-Agent Collaboration for Depressive Symptoms Identification in Memes
paper_authors: Siddhant Agarwal, Adya Dhuler, Polly Ruhnke, Melvin Speisman, Md Shad Akhtar
